pairs: Et afflictus est Jonas afflictione magna,
And Jonah was afflicted with a great affliction,
And he prayed to the Lord,
numquid non hoc est verbum meum cum adhuc essem in terra mea?
propter hoc præoccupavi ut fugerem in Tharsis:
when I was still in my own land?
scio enim quia tu Deus clemens
I knew beforehand to flee into Tarshish.
For I know that you are a lenient and merciful God,
tolle, quæso, animam meam a me,
I ask you to take my life from me.
quia melior est mihi mors quam vita.
For it is better for me to die than to live.”
“Do you really think you are right to be angry?”
Et egressus est Jonas de civitate,
And Jonah went out of the city,
and he sat opposite the east of the city.
And he made himself a shelter there,
et sedebat subter illud in umbra,
and he was sitting under it in the shadow,
until he might see what would befall the city.
And the Lord God prepared an ivy,
and it ascended over the head of Jonah so as to be a shadow over his head,
ut esset umbra super caput ejus,
and to protect him (for he had labored hard).
And Jonah rejoiced because of the ivy,
et lætatus est Jonas super hedera lætitia magna.
Et paravit Deus vermen ascensu diluculi in crastinum:
And God prepared a worm, when dawn approached on the next day,
And when the sun had risen,
præcepit Dominus vento calido et urenti:
the Lord ordered a hot and burning wind.
et percussit sol super caput Jonæ,
And the sun beat down on the head of Jonah,
et petivit animæ suæ ut moreretur,
And he petitioned for his soul that he might die,
Melius est mihi mori quam vivere.
“It is better for me to die than to live.”
And the Lord said to Jonah,
Putasne bene irasceris tu super hedera?
“Do you really think that you are right to be angry because of the ivy?”
Bene irascor ego usque ad mortem.
“I am right to be angry even unto death.”
Tu doles super hederam in qua non laborasti,
for which you have not labored and which you did not cause to grow,
quæ sub una nocte nata est,
though it had been born during one night,
And shall I not spare Nineveh,
in qua sunt plus quam centum viginti millia hominum qui nesciunt quid sit inter dexteram
in which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand men,
who do not know the difference between their right and their left,
